readings: For each patient in the laboratory data, take their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) divided by their average hematocrit (`HCT`), each average ignoring missing values. Keep the patients whose ratio is above the average ratio across all patients, noting how far above it they are. Then, among those, keep the ones whose ratio is also above the average ratio of that kept group, noting how far above this second average they are. Give a single row with the averages, over these final patients, of the ratio, the amount above the overall average, and the amount above the second average, unrounded.
queries:
WITH ratios AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / AVG(HCT) AS ratio
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
    HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) <> 0
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM ratios
),
above_overall AS (
    SELECT r.ID, r.ratio, r.ratio - o.avg_ratio AS diff_overall
    FROM ratios r, overall o
    WHERE r.ratio > o.avg_ratio
),
second AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio2 FROM above_overall
),
final AS (
    SELECT a.ID, a.ratio, a.diff_overall, a.ratio - s.avg_ratio2 AS diff_second
    FROM above_overall a, second s
    WHERE a.ratio > s.avg_ratio2
)
SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       AVG(diff_overall) AS avg_diff_overall,
       AVG(diff_second) AS avg_diff_second
FROM final;
